trust_decision.summary: Whether the email a provider returns is proven verified decides between Registration::provideTrustedEmail (auto-trusted: the login is matched to an existing account with that address) and Registration::suggestEmail (untrusted suggestion); at the pinned commit every provider calls provideTrustedEmail unconditionally, inside its own suggestions() at the provider-to-Flarum Registration boundary, never in the controllers.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Discord, so an engineer opens src/Providers/Discord.php and finds the unconditional provideTrustedEmail at the end of suggestions(); the only nearby guard, verifyEmail at src/Provider.php:76-81, merely rejects null/empty, so the line reads as the sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Twitter is a separate OAuth1 code path with its own controller and no resource-owner payload containing any verification attribute, so after the published fix only touched providers that expose a verified/confirmed field, a solver can read Twitter's unconditional provideTrustedEmail as an accepted design (Twitter returns an already-confirmed account email) rather than an untouched sibling.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Verified-email fast path plus the payload chain must keep working: a genuinely verified provider email must still auto-link/log the user into the existing account, and setPayload()/getPayload() must keep feeding the avatar merge, so an over-broad 'always suggestEmail' (or a rewrite of the shared src/Provider.php helper) breaks login-for-existing-users and avatar assignment. The in-tree integration test's GitLab resource owner carries no confirmed_at, so it also shows the gate demoting a login to a suggestion.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: GitHub's getEmailFromApi already checks primary AND verified (src/Providers/GitHub.php:81-85), so a solver can argue the provider is covered elsewhere and the top-level trust is fine.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared protected helper on the abstract Provider (e.g. trustEmailOrSuggest(Registration, $email, bool $trusted)) that every provider calls
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The base class already owns the shared helpers verifyEmail and provideAvatar, so a maintainer de-duplicating six near-identical suggestions() bodies would naturally land the trust gate here, which then also covers the Twitter path at src/Providers/Twitter.php:70.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A controller-side gate that inspects the resource owner before/after the provider's suggestions() and downgrades the trusted email
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setSuggestions already wraps every provider call and dispatches SettingSuggestions, so it is the obvious place for a cross-provider policy, and a maintainer would then have to duplicate it in src/Controllers/TwitterAuthController.php:125-131.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A getEmailVerified()/isEmailTrustworthy() helper on this in-repo resource owner, with 'email_verified' removed from the requested fields list at src/Providers/Custom/LinkedIn/Provider/LinkedIn.php:42-44
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This class already implements feature-by-feature accessors (getEmail, getFirstName, getId) and its fields array is configurable, so a maintainer could centralise the check there or forget to keep requesting the email_verified field.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A gate on the email-change-on-login job that consults the provider's verification state before writing the provider email onto the linked user
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This job already rewrites a user's email from the provider on every login when update_email_from_provider is on (default true at extend.php:61), so a maintainer extending the same property would have to decide whether an unverified provider email may overwrite the account address.

O9_family: insufficient verification of data authenticity (CWE-345): provider-asserted email trusted without proof, giving account takeover on signup/login
